scope: Visible draft, deployed JSON, October 22 activity window and PR chronology, acceptance/action-evidence claims, Classic Space owner and display gates, LEGO exits, telemetry and draft action candidates. Read-only review; no acceptance, action or scheduling authority.

findings.title: Deployed API reports 12 commits for a 37-commit window
findings.location: Frontmatter summary: “Thirty-seven commits across two repos”; deployed JSON: `commitCount: 12`.
findings.explanation: The collector's author-date rule yields 20 daily-logger and 17 classic-space-venue commits for the consecutive Chicago cutoff interval. Twelve is the number of explicitly listed short SHAs, not the activity total; the source omits explicit commitCount frontmatter.
findings.correction: Keep 37 as the sourced collector count and set explicit commitCount: 37, or rename the 12-value projection as listed commit references.

findings.title: PR #408 is outside the reporting window
findings.location: Daily-logger shipment heading and paragraph, lines 26–28.
findings.explanation: The heading lists ten PRs while the prose says nine. #408 merged at 2026-10-21T01:34:40Z, before the 08:30Z reporting-window start; the remaining nine listed PRs merged inside the interval.
findings.correction: Remove #408 from the in-window shipment heading/time controls or label it explicitly as prior-window context while retaining nine as the in-window count.

findings.title: Fleet-runner ownership is recorded under core #307
findings.location: Decision and roadmap pulse, lines 39–41 and 79.
findings.explanation: The #560 resolution explicitly assigns ownership to fleet-runner under core #307, and #561 asks that owner to accept or reshape the proposal. Individual assignment, acceptance and timing remain open, but initiative ownership is not unknown.
findings.correction: Name fleet-runner under core #307 as owner while separately stating that individual assignment, owner acceptance, a checkpoint and delivery timing remain open.

findings.title: Display composition can proceed through recorded simulation
findings.explanation: Issue #5 explicitly authorizes MBP simulation until the physical 32-inch monitor is available, then requires a later hardware repeat. Issue #6 defines split-pane and phone-sized remote-browser work. Physical validation is a later gate, not a wholesale blocker on composition work.
findings.correction: Separate immediately available MBP/narrow-viewport simulation work from later physical-monitor and real-remote-device verification.

findings.title: LEGO drafts have distinct documented exit gates
findings.explanation: #44 and #46 are non-operative overlays with close-or-supersede exits and complete-cut/preflight requirements. #45 is the HOUSE-WORLD R0 study and instead requires a second-steward register check followed by James's merge decision; it is not titled DO NOT MERGE.
findings.correction: Preserve close/supersede plus complete-cut/preflight exits for #44/#46 and the separate second-steward plus James decision gate for #45.

findings.title: Current events contradict the frozen telemetry premise
findings.location: Roadmap telemetry paragraph and `/resolve skill-telemetry-stream` draft candidate, lines 85 and 96–102.
findings.explanation: Immutable sources contain October 20 invocation/follow-through events and October 21 disposition events. A later native replay reports one of fourteen suggestions followed, while qualifying the unavailable exact generation payload. The new candidate is awaiting review, not admitted, and rests on a false blanket-freeze premise; older telemetry validation act-2026-04-12-validate-c53d7a is already closed as superseded.
findings.correction: Remove the blanket freeze claim, retain source/freshness limits and actual replay ratios, and reject or rewrite the awaiting-review candidate around a specific unresolved telemetry problem without reopening completed work.

findings.title: The Chicago-over-UTC rationale is unsupported
findings.explanation: #408 establishes the consecutive Chicago cutoff, DST behavior, guard and unchanged schedules, but does not record the article's historical rationale that UTC was rejected to preserve the operator's morning boundary.
findings.correction: Keep the adopted interval and actual run receipt; attribute the rationale only to a primary operator decision and keep trigger, start, completion, merge and public availability separate.

findings.title: The claimed prior Codex scope incident lacks a primary record
findings.explanation: PR #3 proves the instruction relocation and current boundary, but does not identify the asserted earlier incident, generated code, receipt or correction in which Codex allegedly treated scene instructions as fleet governance.
findings.correction: Keep the source-backed instruction-boundary change, but remove the incident claim or link the exact primary failure and correction record.
